session_id_policy.offline_rule: Bridge may generate a collision-resistant session_id before network availability. Backend must reject collisions, but must not silently remap an accepted offline session ID because queued events already reference it.

NO_SESSION.description: No active or recoverable gameplay session is bound to the client.

STARTING.description: Session identity/context is being committed. Gameplay evidence must not begin until the session has a durable local context.

OPEN.description: Normal connected session. Canonical events may be validated and transmitted live.

OPEN_OFFLINE.description: Session continues without backend connectivity. Canonical event bodies are created normally and persisted locally.

REPLAYING.description: Queued immutable events are being submitted in original order. New gameplay may continue, but newly created events stay behind the backlog until earlier evidence is resolved.

ENDING.description: Gameplay evidence creation has stopped. Remaining accepted/queued evidence is flushed and the canonical session.ended fact is finalised.

CLOSED.description: Session is immutable and closed. New gameplay facts cannot be attached.

transitions.guard: durable session context established and connectivity available
offline mode permitted and durable local session context established
no gameplay evidence has been accepted

state_mutations.effect: end_requested=true; remain OPEN_OFFLINE until connectivity returns and queued evidence can replay
end_requested=true; remain REPLAYING until backlog drains
remain ENDING; persist finalisation work and retry when connectivity returns
return idempotent already-accepted/already-closed receipt when identity matches; never append a duplicate fact

event_acceptance.ENDING: ERR-SES-002 for newly created gameplay events; existing queued/final lifecycle evidence may flush
event_acceptance.CLOSED: ERR-SES-003 for new evidence; exact duplicate retries may receive idempotent acknowledgement

offline_queue.ordering: local queue sequence, with canonical timestamp retained as occurrence time
replay_policy: Submit oldest unresolved queued event first.
Do not mint a new event_id during replay.
Do not replace the original occurrence timestamp with upload time.
Backend records receipt time separately from canonical occurrence timestamp.
Accepted or duplicate-confirmed events leave the queue.
Permanent validation failures move to retained sync-failure evidence for QA rather than being silently discarded.
offline_queue.offline_session_start: When a session begins offline, session.started is created as canonical evidence and durably queued before gameplay evidence; offline_start_committed changes state only after that durable write succeeds.

crash_recovery.rule: A process restart does not silently resume gameplay into the old session. Recover/persist the old session evidence, close it as interrupted, then create a new session for new gameplay.
procedure: Load durable session and queue metadata.
If queued evidence exists and connectivity is available, replay it using original event IDs/timestamps.
Move to ENDING after recoverable evidence is resolved.
Emit/finalise session.ended with an interruption end_reason.
Start a fresh session_id for subsequent gameplay.

complete_when: session.ended accepted or canonical closure evidence recorded
complete_with_sync_issues_when: one or more permanent validation/sync failures retained as QA evidence

errors.name: UNKNOWN_SESSION
errors.meaning: session_id does not resolve to a known session.

errors.name: INVALID_SESSION_STATE
errors.meaning: Command or event is not permitted in the session's current lifecycle state.

errors.name: SESSION_CLOSED
errors.meaning: New canonical evidence cannot be appended to a closed session.

errors.name: BUILD_SESSION_MISMATCH
errors.meaning: Event build_id does not match the immutable build_id bound to the session.

errors.name: INSTALLATION_SESSION_MISMATCH
errors.meaning: Event installation_id does not match the installation bound to the session.

errors.name: SESSION_START_CONFLICT
errors.meaning: A new incompatible session.start was requested while another session context is starting/open/recoverable.

session_start.same_session_same_context: Return the existing STARTING/current session context. Do not create another session.

session_end.ENDING: Return current ending status; do not emit a second session.ended fact.
session_end.CLOSED: Return already-closed receipt when the same session identity is retried; do not mutate the session.
session_end.OPEN_OFFLINE_or_REPLAYING: Set/retain end_requested=true; do not create a second close request.

idempotence.event_retry: An exact retry with the same event_id represents the same fact. Accepted duplicates receive an idempotent receipt rather than a second stored event.
